使用 systems-paper-review，只读审查下面这篇完整的短论文。必须先检查论文贡献类型、整体 claim-evidence 链和每个章节，再逐段、逐句、逐词检查；显式列出每个正常与异常单位的 coverage 状态，并给 coverage receipt。每一段都要识别实际角色，并用已有的段落角色惯例检查 opening、development 和 payoff/handoff。不要改写。

# Atlas: Predictable Recovery for Interactive Storage

## Introduction

Interactive storage must recover quickly enough to preserve request latency after a crash. In our target service, replaying a long log delays admission of new requests. This delay makes bounded recovery a design requirement.

Existing systems periodically checkpoint the full index. Because checkpoint cost grows with index size, operators lengthen the checkpoint interval. The longer interval leaves the recovery-time requirement unmet.

Our key observation is that only entries newer than the last validated frontier require replay. Tracking that frontier changes recovery from a full-index operation into a suffix operation. The design must therefore preserve and validate the frontier before acknowledging an update.

This principle leaves one operational question: how does Atlas update the frontier without serializing foreground requests? The next section must identify the relevant state and ordering rule. That rule is the bridge from the insight to a concrete mechanism.

## Overview

Atlas separates foreground logging from frontier validation. A background validator advances a durable frontier only after checking the corresponding suffix, while readers continue to use the previous frontier. Recovery begins at the latest durable frontier and replays the remaining suffix.

## Design

The validator reads the next suffix, checks each record checksum, and atomically stores the new frontier. If validation fails, it retains the previous frontier and reports the corrupt suffix. Thus, every published frontier identifies a checked replay prefix.

## Evaluation

We compare Atlas with full-index checkpointing on a 64 GiB index. Atlas sustains 1.2 million operations per second, while the baseline sustains 1.0 million. This experiment establishes the throughput effect under the tested steady-state workload.

## Limitations

Our prototype evaluates only steady-state throughput on one server. It does not measure crash-recovery time, tail latency during validation, or multi-server failure behavior. The evidence therefore does not yet establish the bounded-recovery claim stated in the introduction.
